title: Which of the two weights is heavier?
description: A fraction of five hundred grams is compared with a fraction of four kilograms. Both weights are written in grams, worked out by shortening, and compared.
teaching_notes: One idea: put both weights in the same unit before comparing, and shorten before multiplying to find a fraction of a weight. Watch for students who compare the fractions without changing kilograms to grams.

video_script.why: The child uses the shorten before multiplying method of the solved example to compare two weights.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question, twelve fifteenths of five hundred grams and three twentieths of four kilograms
video_script.anchor: two weights on the pans of a balance
video_script.payoff_line: Three twentieths of four kilograms is heavier, at six hundred grams against four hundred grams

final_answer.value: 3/20 of 4 kg is heavier: 600 g against 400 g
final_answer.spoken: three twentieths of four kilograms is heavier

maths_rules: 600 g > 400 g, so 3/20 of 4 kg is heavier
check: 12/15 is less than 1, so the first weight is less than 500 g
video_script.design: Two weights on a balance. Each weight is worked out on the board in grams and then set on its pan.
